documents.title: H&P - Admission - Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time seen: 21:40, ED bed 7. Admitted to stepdown.
Chief complaint: cough, fever, new confusion x 2 days.
HPI:
67 yo F brought to ED by son for cough productive of rusty sputum, fevers to 102F at home, and progressive dyspnea over 3 days.
New confusion per son, who reports patient is normally independent - drives, manages her own medications, lives alone.
Son states she was mixing up his name with her brother's since yesterday evening and did not eat today.
Oriented to self only on arrival. Does not know place or approximate time.
Reports pleuritic right-sided chest pain with coughing. Two episodes of vomiting today, unable to keep fluids down.
No chest pressure at rest, no orthopnea, no PND, no leg swelling. No recent travel. No sick contacts known to son.
ROS: limited by mental status; per son - chills, poor appetite, generalized weakness. No hematuria, no rash, no diarrhea.
PMH:
HTN, hyperlipidemia, type 2 DM (diet controlled), osteoarthritis, remote tobacco use 20 pack-years quit ~15 yrs ago.
No prior pneumonia, no COPD, no known CHF.
PSH: cholecystectomy, TAH.
Home meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, HCTZ 25 mg daily, acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: lives alone in single-level home, son nearby. No alcohol, no illicit drugs.
Family hx: father MI age 70, mother stroke.
ED COURSE / VITALS:
Triage 19:52 - T 38.9C, HR 118 irregular-regular, BP 86/54, RR 32, SpO2 87% on RA.
Hypotension to 86/54 at triage; 2 L normal saline given wide open via 18g x2.
BP after fluids 96/58 at 21:05. HR down to 104.
SpO2 87% on RA at triage; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%.
Respiratory rate 32 at triage, 30 at 4 hours.
Blood cultures x2 drawn prior to antibiotics. Sputum sent. Urine legionella and pneumococcal antigen sent.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Gen: ill-appearing elderly female, mildly diaphoretic, using accessory muscles intermittently.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no JVD.
Lungs: bronchial breath sounds and coarse crackles right base and right axilla, dullness to percussion right base, egophony present.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, cap refill 3 sec.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no edema, warm.
Neuro: arouses to voice, follows simple commands, oriented to self only, no focal deficit, no neck stiffness.
Skin: no rash.
DATA:
WBC 18.6 with 12% bands, Hgb 12.1, Plt 214.
BUN 34 mg/dL, sodium 127 mEq/L on arrival. Creatinine 1.4, K 3.6, glucose 168, bicarb 20.
Lactate 3.1. Procalcitonin 4.8.
VBG pH 7.44, pCO2 33.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
EKG: sinus tachycardia, no acute ST changes.
ASSESSMENT:
67 yo F with severe community-acquired pneumonia, RML/RLL, complicated by hypotension, hypoxemia, acute encephalopathy, hyponatremia and prerenal azotemia.
CURB-65 of 3 (confusion, BUN >19, RR >=30). Warrants inpatient care with close monitoring; stepdown bed.
Hyponatremia likely combination of poor intake, vomiting, HCTZ, and possible SIADH from pneumonia.
PLAN:
1. CAP - ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin, started 21:15 in ED. Continue blood/sputum cultures, urinary antigens pending.
2. Hypoxemia - continue 3L NC, titrate for SpO2 >92%. Incentive spirometry q1h while awake. RT to assess.
3. Hypotension - additional 500 mL NS bolus if MAP <65, reassess. Hold lisinopril and HCTZ.
4. Confusion - likely infectious/metabolic. Delirium precautions, frequent reorientation, avoid sedatives, bed alarm.
5. Hyponatremia/BUN - recheck BMP at 04:00, trend Na. Gentle IV fluids.
6. Vomiting - NPO for now, ondansetron 4 mg IV q6h PRN. IV route for all meds.
7. Effusion - small, no tap tonight; repeat imaging if worsening or persistent fever.
8. DVT ppx: enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily. Tele monitoring.
Son updated at bedside 22:10, all questions answered.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:20
Subjective: Pt awake, states she is in a hospital but still unsure of month. Son at bedside reports she is more conversant than last night.
Coughing productive of yellow sputum. Vomited once overnight at 03:40 after sips of water.
Still on 3L NC on hospital day 2. Reports breathing easier than at admission.
I/O: 2.1 L in / 1.3 L out. Weight up 1.2 kg.
Exam:
Gen: less toxic appearing, no accessory muscle use at rest.
Lungs: crackles right base persist, decreased breath sounds right base, no wheeze on left.
CV: tachy, regular, no murmur.
Abd: soft, nontender. Neuro: oriented to self and place, not time; no focal deficit.
Labs 05:15: WBC 15.2 (from 18.6), Na 130, BUN 29, Cr 1.1, K 3.8, lactate 1.6.
Blood cultures NGTD at 12h. Sputum gram stain: gram positive diplococci, many WBCs. Urine pneumococcal antigen positive, legionella negative.
Assessment: Severe CAP, likely pneumococcal, improving hemodynamically. Encephalopathy improving. Hyponatremia and azotemia improving with hydration.
Plan:
1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin; unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so all abx remain IV.
2. O2: continue 3L NC, wean as tolerated, target SpO2 >92%. Ambulate with RN and check saturation with activity.
3. Antiemetics scheduled ondansetron 4 mg IV q8h, advance to clears if no emesis by afternoon.
4. Continue to hold lisinopril and HCTZ. Repeat BMP in AM.
5. Delirium precautions, mobilize out of bed to chair, sleep hygiene.
6. Chest imaging to be repeated if fever persists past 48h or oxygen requirement rises.
7. Continue enoxaparin ppx, incentive spirometry q1h awake.
Discussed with son 08:05. Attending rounded, agrees with plan.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD3
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD3 07:05
Subjective: Pt feels much better. No vomiting in past 20 hours, tolerated full clear liquids and half a breakfast tray.
Cough looser, less pleuritic pain. Walked hallway approx 100 ft with RN yesterday evening.
Oriented to self, place, and month. Son states she sounds like herself.
Vitals: Tmax 37.4C, Tcurr 36.9C, HR 82-94, BP 118/70, RR 18-20.
SpO2 94-96% on 2L NC overnight, weaned to RA at 06:30 with SpO2 93% at rest and 91% with ambulation.
I/O: 1.6 L in / 1.85 L out. Weight down 0.8 kg.
Exam:
Gen: comfortable, sitting in chair, no distress.
Lungs: crackles right base decreased, no bronchial breath sounds today, dullness persists at right base.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Abd soft. Ext no edema.
Neuro: alert, fully conversant, no focal deficit.
Blood cultures x2: no growth at 36h.
Assessment: Pneumococcal CAP improving. Oxygenation, mental status, sodium and renal function all trending to baseline.
Plan:
1. Transition to oral antibiotic therapy today now that PO tolerated; stop IV azithromycin after oral dose given.
2. O2: continue trial on room air, keep SpO2 >92%, recheck ambulatory saturation this afternoon with PT.
3. PT/OT eval for safe discharge home - lives alone.
4. Resume lisinopril at half dose today if BP remains >110 systolic; continue holding HCTZ until outpatient recheck.
5. Diet advance to regular, encourage intake.
6. Continue incentive spirometry, mobilize TID.
7. Anticipate discharge tomorrow if afebrile, stable on RA, and ambulating safely.
Attending rounded, agrees. Son updated by phone 09:10.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD4
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitting diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, severe.
Discharge diagnoses: 1. Pneumococcal community-acquired pneumonia, right middle and right lower lobe, with small parapneumonic effusion. 2. Acute encephalopathy, resolved. 3. Hyponatremia, resolved.
Length of stay: 4 days, discharged HD4 at 14:20.
BRIEF COURSE:
67 yo F presented with 3 days of cough, fever and dyspnea. New confusion per son, who reports patient is normally independent; she was oriented to self only on arrival.
Triage vitals notable for SpO2 87% on RA at triage; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%. Respiratory rate 32 at triage, 30 at 4 hours.
Hypotension to 86/54 at triage; 2 L normal saline given; BP after fluids 96/58.
Labs on arrival: WBC 18.6 with 12% bands, BUN 34 mg/dL, sodium 127 mEq/L on arrival, lactate 3.1.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note; admitted to stepdown for monitoring.
Treated with ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin; unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so therapy remained IV.
Urine pneumococcal antigen positive; legionella negative. Sputum with gram positive diplococci. Blood cultures x2 no growth at time of discharge.
Still on 3L NC on hospital day 2; weaned to 2L on HD2 evening and to room air HD3 morning.
Mental status returned to baseline by HD3. Sodium corrected to 136 and BUN to 15 by HD4 with hydration and holding diuretic.
Ambulatory saturation HD4 95% on room air over 250 ft with PT; PT cleared for home without equipment.
DISCHARGE VITALS: T 36.8C, HR 78, BP 122/72, RR 17, SpO2 95% RA.
DISCHARGE EXAM: alert and fully oriented, comfortable, scattered fine crackles right base, no accessory muscle use, no edema.
DISCHARGE LABS: WBC 8.2, Hgb 11.8, Na 136, K 4.1, BUN 15, Cr 0.9.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
- Oral antibiotic to complete a total 7-day course, last dose in 3 days.
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily (reduced from 20 mg).
- Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly.
- Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h PRN pain or fever.
- HCTZ held; do not restart until reviewed at follow-up.
- Guaifenesin PRN cough.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Use incentive spirometer 10 times per hour while awake for 2 weeks. Walk several times daily.
Drink fluids, eat regularly, weigh daily.
Return for fever >100.4F, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, new confusion, vomiting, or lightheadedness.
FOLLOW-UP:
Primary care in 5-7 days for exam, repeat BMP, and blood pressure/medication review.
Repeat chest x-ray in 6-8 weeks to document resolution of the infiltrate and effusion.
Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination to be addressed at follow-up.
Son present at discharge teaching 13:50 and will stay with patient for the first several nights. Verbalized understanding.
